analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | tough EPS start 14 Oct 2026
key_insights: Industrials fell 140bps on 10/14/26, underperforming the broader market (down 80bps). Materials fell 60bps. CPI was the main driver of the sell-off, with the 10-year yield spiking to 5.25%.
Staples and healthcare led while technology and communications lagged. Quality outperformed on the factor board, while beta and high-beta momentum were hit.
Within industrials, defense and aerospace held up relatively well, while data center, airlines and housing sold off.

Client inbounds focused on why AI/data center names sold off so much: DPC weakness several days in a row, feedback to the TT upgrade and CARR/LII downgrade, the setup into JBHT, and GEV weakness in particular.
Other client questions: relative strength in HXL, RTX, HWM, HEI and GE, whether MMM is shorted or owned, and the magnitude of CDNL's move over the last few days.

September core CPI rose 0.33%, above expectations. Shelter was firmer than expected, with OER up 0.35% m/m and adding about 5bp more to core than GS expected. OER strength was concentrated in the Midwest (+0.68%, SA by GS).
Travel services, autos and recreation goods were also firm in the CPI report.

GS estimates September core PCE rose 0.32%, versus its 0.20% expectation before the CPI release, for a year-over-year rate of +3.09%. The revision reflects upside surprises in OER, hotels and recreation.

The GS Quality Pair Index (GSP1QUAL), neutral to sector, industry and factor, is up 20% over 3 months to a 12m high on about 13% realized vol. The move was driven by a sharp selloff in the short leg (GSX1BFQS).

GS argues the market is rewarding quality because of a shift in focus from growth to the composition of growth. Growth in AI and non-AI pockets should decelerate over the next 12 months, which tends to favor quality.
Quality can hedge AI, momentum or beta exposure given its strong negative correlation to those crowded themes. Momentum positioning is at the 78th percentile on 5y and beta at the 81st.

Quality technicals are stretched, with RSI at 83 after the factor rose in 16 of the last 18 sessions. A softer CPI print or evidence that rates are peaking could trigger a reversal and a relief rally in longer-duration, lower-quality names.
Cyclical earnings started tough, though reactions were muted (RPM +3%, FAST +1%, DAL flat) and the underlying data was soft. GS likes the setup for RPM and is more cautious on DAL and FAST.

RPM reported a miss, with fiscal Q2 and full-year guidance lower. It cited broad consumer weakness, price/cost pressure, slowing education and healthcare markets, and product shortages from supplier raw material issues. CPG is very volume sensitive. Energy and infrastructure were strong in PCG, and the company is leaning into share repurchase.

DAL missed and cut guidance. RASM accelerated in Q4 but TSA data has turned negative. Open questions: demand elasticity, whether CASMx can trend to low single digits in 2027, and the RASM/CASM spread in 2027 given no industry bankruptcies.

FAST's headline beat was driven by one-time benefits, alongside a September topline slowdown. Data centers drive about a third of growth. The company calls September normal course rather than an economic slowdown. Pricing of 2.4% slowed sequentially and will be a smaller driver in 2027 than 2026. Q3 gross margin got a 40bps benefit from sourcing savings, supplier rebates and tariff effects, of which 20bps was timing related.

earnings_insights: RPM (reported 10/14/26): miss versus expectations, fiscal Q2 and full-year guidance lower. Stock +3% on the day. No EPS figures given.
DAL (reported 10/14/26): miss and guidance cut. Stock flat on the day. No EPS figures given.

FAST (reported 10/14/26, pre-market): headline beat driven by one-time benefits. September topline slowed. Pricing of 2.4% slowed sequentially, and Q3 gross margin had a 40bps benefit, of which 20bps was timing related. Stock +1% on the day.
JBHT is scheduled to report post-market on 10/15/26. GS calls out the setup into the print.
